description: Host-supplied strings that reach a CSS value — a colour prop, an inline style binding, a custom-property override. CSS injection rarely executes script on a current engine; what it reliably does is exfiltrate (an attribute-selector plus a `url()` leaks a value one request at a time), overlay (position a transparent element over a real control) and erase (paint a security-relevant element out of existence). The required outcome for a style sink is `escaped`: the value stays in the one declaration it was given and cannot open a second one.

fixtures.title: closing one declaration to start another
fixtures.rationale: The base case for any prop whose value is concatenated into a style string. When the value is set through an element attribute or a Vue `:style` object the semicolon is data and the whole declaration is simply invalid, which is `escaped`; when it is concatenated into a stylesheet it is a second declaration.
fixtures.provenance: OWASP CSS-injection guidance; standard style-context test.

fixtures.title: legacy IE expression() value
fixtures.rationale: Dead on every supported engine, kept for the same reason as `vbscript:` in the URL file: it distinguishes a component that validates its CSS values from one that happens not to be attacked by the vectors somebody remembered.
fixtures.provenance: OWASP filter-evasion cheat sheet, CSS section.

fixtures.title: url() pointing off-origin
fixtures.rationale: The realistic CSS attack in a component library: no script, one request, and whatever the selector could distinguish is now known off-origin. It is also the case that shows a component's CSS surface is governed by the host's CSP `img-src`/`default-src` and not by anything the component can decide alone.

fixtures.title: closing a style element and opening a script
fixtures.rationale: For any value written into a `<style>` element rather than an attribute — the theme-injection path. The tokenizer leaves the style element on the literal `</style`, so quoting inside CSS does not contain it.
fixtures.provenance: HTML Standard raw-text end-tag tokenizer states; cure53 style-context cases.
